last_committee_decision.bear_thesis: The trade fails because the three cited drivers are either lagging, non-predictive, or contradicted by the only forward-looking metric in the dataset. The Sentinel net bias of -5 (Short 15 vs Long 10) is a sentiment snapshot with no demonstrated predictive validity for INFY — it reflects positioning, not alpha. The FII outflow of ₹9,484.2 Cr over 30 days is a known, stale flow; at ~₹316 Cr/day, it is dwarfed by average daily volume (not available, but INFY typically trades ₹2,000–4,000 Cr/day), meaning the market has likely already absorbed this supply. The bearish MACD is a lagging trend-follower on a stock trading with RSI 44.88 (neutral) and no 200DMA breach — it signals the past, not the next move. With PCR at 1.0 (neutral), OI and dealer mode not available, and macro regime RISK_OFF at only 65% confidence, there is no leading-edge confirmation. The failure mechanism: a mean-reversion bounce from oversold sentiment/flow conditions into a neutral PCR environment, triggered by any positive catalyst (earnings, rupee strength, sector rotation), which the data shows no defense against.
bull_wins: verified institutional flow signal — not noise — and directionally consistent with the short thesis. (2) Sentinel net bias of -5 (Short 15 vs Long 10) reflects a measurable sentiment tilt from a proprietary model
even if its predictive validity is unproven.
bear_wins: Dealer mode UNKNOWN — the only live derivative metric is neutral
contradicting actionable smart-money conviction for a short. (2) No Monte Carlo base rate means the
7% friction cost cannot be evaluated against expected edge
the Bull's 58% confidence has no statistical floor
making the trade a "hope dressed in data" per the Bear's one-line.
last_committee_decision.committee_verdict: SKIP — we are shorting on a -5 sentiment score, ₹9.5k Cr of stale FII selling, and a lagging MACD with neutral PCR, no OI, no dealer view, and no Monte Carlo floor; the 1.7% friction cost cannot be justified against an unknown base rate, and the Bear's structural critique that three lagging signals ≠ edge remains unrefuted.
